description: Bug report from a user of packaging: Requirement("name @ https://example.com/name.whl\nevil==1") is accepted. Its url is "https://example.com/name.whl\nevil==1", and str() of the requirement writes "evil==1" as a second line, which a requirements file reads as another requirement. Find the problem and fix it. Change src/packaging/ only.
environment: Python >= 3.13 stdlib; base tree = pypa/packaging 2602dd0^ (src, tests, LICENSE*, README, pyproject, .gitignore) plus the task-owned helper bench_fixtures/req.py; no repository history; the project's own test suite needs pytest, which is not installed
visible_checks: python -c "from src.packaging.requirements import Requirement; print(Requirement('name @ https://example.com/name.whl ; os_name == \"nt\"'))" (from the workspace root; pytest is not available)
provenance: real fix: pypa/packaging commit 2602dd0 (fix(parser): reject whitespace in the URL token, #1379, 2026-10-01); reference/good.patch is that commit's src/ diff; symptom-only description (one URL with an embedded LF); hidden cases authored for agent-benchmark (2026-10-18): CR, CRLF and LF in other positions plus guards; only line breaks are tested, because the base's tests already reject a line-break suffix and its grammar's whitespace is space and tab (other whitespace is an undocumented choice); other reference patches built by build_task.py. Public repository: contamination possible
